sourceEvidence.label: CostWeave v0.5.8.1 privileged boundary source review

assessment.summary: Secret, network, redaction, project and replay invariants should share one owned enforcement boundary before stable Adapters are added.

nonNegotiables: Default installation performs zero external calls.
No secret value is persisted or returned by a public API.
A project cannot enumerate another project's runs or artifacts.
An ambiguous external side effect is not automatically repeated.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
v0.5.8.2 remains a single-process, loopback-only control plane.

opportunities.title: Centralize privileged Adapter and data-scope enforcement
opportunities.summary: Give one versioned boundary ownership of Adapter manifests, secret leases, endpoint admission, prompt risk, project scope, redaction and side-effect identity.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current controls are useful but dispersed; callers can acquire ambient environment and network authority or return global data without passing one common policy object.

evidence.claim: HTTP adapters read configured environment variables directly and construct Authorization headers inside the execution path.
Logical external calls have reservation idempotency, but Provider idempotency forwarding and an append-only side-effect contract are not centrally represented.
Evidence export owns a local recursive redactor with a limited key and Bearer-prefix vocabulary.
Run, approval, task and artifact reads are loopback-protected but not filtered by a project security scope.
Without a project identifier in the durable run request, project ownership cannot survive restart as part of the authoritative projection.

desiredInvariants: Only a versioned registered Adapter manifest can request network or secret capabilities.
Secrets are resolved by short-lived leases and never enter config, persistence, logs, errors or exports.
Remote endpoints are explicit HTTPS targets, redirects and private-address targets are rejected, and response size is bounded.
Every run and derived Artifact is visible only inside its durable project scope.
Prompt-like untrusted data cannot expand tools, authority or scope; suspicious override instructions fail closed without a separate approval.
Every external side effect has an immutable project-scoped identity and either Provider idempotency or an explicit compensation strategy.

options.title: Strengthen local guards
options.summary: Extend checks in the current Adapter, server and exporter without a common policy owner.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Direct checks narrow known paths but ambient authority remains distributed.
Route filters can cover current endpoints but future endpoints may omit them.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known call sites gain checks, while ownership drift remains possible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Trace every secret, network and run-data entry point.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local checks add no service hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark request and Adapter admission latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded temporary values are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS during export and Adapter fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known unsafe inputs fail earlier, but policy behavior can diverge.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a shared negative corpus against every call site.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new component exists, but audit state remains fragmented.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review incident reconstruction from logs and SQLite.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small compatibility-preserving patches are easy to roll back.

residualRisks: Future connectors can omit one or more local guards.

workPackages: Patch local guards and add negative tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Known negative cases fail before privileged operations.

options.title: Central security boundary
options.summary: Introduce one policy, broker and append-only store consumed by Adapters, exports and HTTP project gates.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adapters receive leases and admission decisions from the boundary.
Append-only side-effect identity complements the existing call reservation.
One redactor is reused for API, logs and exports.
Durable project scope is enforced before run-derived reads or writes.
Project and residency become part of the persisted RunRequest.

tradeoffs.assessment: Privileged capabilities and data scope share one fail-closed owner.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run negative endpoint, secret, injection, project and replay tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Admission adds bounded hashing, pattern matching and SQLite writes around external calls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare P50/P95 admission latency against v0.5.8.1 fixtures; investigate if P95 exceeds 10 ms locally.

tradeoffs.assessment: Registries and secret leases are bounded and contain no retained response bodies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS over 10,000 admissions and exports.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ambiguous side effects stop in reserved state instead of automatic replay; central failures are fail closed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject crashes before and after transport completion and verify no second transport call.

tradeoffs.assessment: One public policy and count surface simplifies audit, with a new migration and event vocabulary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reconstruct a fixture call from security and external-call receipts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Run projections and API scope gain compatible defaulted fields; all run-derived routes require audit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Hydrate old snapshots and run the full historical suite.

residualRisks: Single-process isolation cannot contain malicious in-process plugin code.
Logical project revocation does not physically erase historical SQLite rows.

workPackages: Route Adapter admission and secret leases through them.
Add API, UI and regression coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Secret leak corpus has zero public or persistent occurrences.
Unauthorized network and tools perform zero transport calls.
Cross-project runs and artifacts return not found.
Side-effect identity replay is idempotent and conflicting reuse is rejected.
migrationNotes: Default old project scope to local-default.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable new Adapter entry points, retain migration records, and run v0.5.8.1 with local-default compatibility.

options.title: Isolated Adapter gateway
options.summary: Move credentials and outbound network into a separate least-privileged process or service.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The orchestrator no longer holds Provider credentials or raw network authority.
Gateway isolation does not itself enforce local API project scope.

tradeoffs.assessment: A process boundary narrows credential and network blast radius.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt capability escape from a deliberately hostile plugin fixture.

tradeoffs.assessment: IPC serialization and another queue enter each external call.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end P50/P95 with realistic payload sizes.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second runtime and bounded queues consume additional memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure combined working set under idle and burst load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Plugin crashes are isolated, but gateway availability becomes a dependency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Kill and restart the gateway during calls and verify reconciliation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deployment, health, version skew and credential rotation become multi-process concerns.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform install, upgrade, rollback and incident drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adapter calls need a versioned IPC protocol and deployment packaging.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run dual-path Shadow traffic before cutover.

residualRisks: The local API and project data boundary still need central enforcement.

acceptanceCriteria: Host process cannot read Provider secrets or open arbitrary outbound connections.
migrationNotes: Defer to v0.6 production connector work.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return traffic to the in-process boundary while keeping Adapters default off.

opportunities.recommendation: Implement the central boundary in v0.5.8.2; revisit process isolation before accepting untrusted production plugins.

openQuestions: What verified physical-erasure SLA will future multi-tenant deployments require?
What Adapter admission P95 is acceptable under real concurrency?
